experiment: Optimized run_frame_general_until disassembly across the no-TLS StackGuard candidate
finding: The control-path machine code changes across the candidate build. Alignment alone cannot explain its retired-instruction movement, but this comparison does not establish global inlining as the sole cause.

host.resource_limits: No container memory or CPU quota reported

build.command: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/candidate-{a,b} CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_PRODUCTION_DEBUG=true CARGO_PROFILE_PRODUCTION_STRIP=none cargo build --locked --offline --profile production -p quench-node --bin quench-node
build.profile_policy_note: Cargo.toml declares release LTO as fat and production inherits release. /Users/admin/.cargo/config.toml overrides profile.release lto to thin; the verbose candidate rustc command confirms the effective thin-LTO flag. Both compared builds used thin LTO, so their comparison is matched, but it does not test the declared fat-LTO policy.

assembly.tool: otool -tV; source attribution checked with atos -inlineFrames

static_instruction_count.counting_rule: Count disassembly lines in the extracted symbol body that begin with a 16-digit address and instruction mnemonic.

stack_addressed_instruction_count.counting_rule: Among the counted instruction lines, count operands containing [sp or [x29.

assembly.incdec_observation: The source-mapped Op::IncDec boolean-flag decode has 7 instructions in the baseline and 8 in the candidate; the candidate adds a nop on the loop's index++ path. In the checked_sub overflow path, the baseline emits b.vs while the candidate emits an unconditional b to a differently laid-out continuation.
assembly.local_opcode_observation: The sampled LoadLocalPlain body has the same five load/address instructions plus its shared-result branch in both builds. The sampled StoreLocalPlain body has the same instruction count. Register assignments and addresses differ.
assembly.interpretation: Compiled dispatch code changed, including a repeated IncDec path. The added nop cannot by itself account for the measured +1.2032% retired-instruction change; other changed hot paths remain unattributed. Differences in static call counts and stack traffic show whole-function codegen changes, but this disassembly alone does not identify a particular LLVM inlining decision as the root cause.

measurement.interpretation: The no-TLS StackGuard candidate was inconclusive because the unrelated control moved more than the target cycle delta. This disassembly independently confirms machine-code drift; it does not convert that candidate into a performance win.

follow_up_policy.inlining_annotations: No broad inline/noinline annotations were added. Inspect and attribute additional changed hot paths before making a reviewed annotation list.
follow_up_policy.small_change_gate: For candidates below roughly 3%, compare target and control movement in the same campaign and prefer fixture-level pairs; retired instructions are attribution, while cycles or elapsed time decide retention.
follow_up_policy.alignment: Test alignment flags as a separate experiment after machine-code drift is understood.
